Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the InnovaTech Solutions First Quarter Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Sarah Chen, Investor Relations Manager. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen, Investor Relations Manager:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to InnovaTech Solutions’ first quarter earnings call. Joining me today are Dr. Anya Sharma, CEO; David Lee, CFO; and Michael Rodriguez, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Dr. Sharma.

Dr. Anya Sharma, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Sarah. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

This quarter, we’ve made significant capital expenditure investments, totaling KRW 10.7 trillion. This allocation is designed to fortify our long-term competitive advantage and address anticipated future demand across key business segments. This is slightly higher than our initial projections of KRW 10.5 trillion, primarily due to accelerated investments in advanced node foundry capacity.

We’re seeing challenges on the wafer ASP front, driven primarily by oversupply in both the DRAM and NAND markets. While we anticipated price erosion, the magnitude of the declines, particularly in NAND, was slightly more pronounced than our initial forecasts.

These results reflect our strategy in action. I’ll now hand it over to David Lee to discuss the financials.

David Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Dr. Sharma, and hello, everyone.

Let’s take a closer look at the numbers:

As Dr. Sharma mentioned, we’ve seen some headwinds on the wafer ASP front this quarter. Overall wafer ASP experienced a significant decline, driven primarily by oversupply in both the DRAM and NAND markets. While we anticipated price erosion, the magnitude of the declines, particularly in NAND, was slightly more pronounced than our initial forecasts. This is attributable to a confluence of factors, including inventory correction by our customers, macroeconomic headwinds, aggressive pricing strategies from competitors, and yield improvements and process maturity. Despite these challenges, we actively managed our product mix, prioritized higher-margin applications, and focused on cost optimization initiatives to mitigate the impact of the ASP declines. We also continued to ramp up production of our next-generation technologies, which we believe will offer a performance and cost advantage in the coming quarters.

Furthermore, our consolidated revenue for the quarter reached KRW 63.7 trillion. This represents a significant 9.5% sequential decline (QoQ) compared to the KRW 70.4 trillion reported in the previous quarter. On a year-over-year basis (YoY), the revenue shows a decrease of 7.2% from the KRW 68.6 trillion recorded in the same quarter last year. The DX division, encompassing mobile communications, visual display, and digital appliances, demonstrated resilience and achieved positive revenue growth, primarily driven by the successful launch and strong initial sales of our new flagship smartphone models, the Galaxy Z Fold 6 and Galaxy Z Flip 6. However, the Memory business and other component businesses experienced a more pronounced decline in revenue, significantly impacting the overall consolidated figures. Memory business revenue amounted to KRW 18.5 trillion, a steep 20% QoQ decrease, and other components (including System LSI and Foundry) revenue totaled KRW 7 trillion, a 15% QoQ decline. In the previous quarter's earnings call, we provided a consolidated revenue guidance range of KRW 68 trillion to KRW 72 trillion for this quarter. The actual revenue of KRW 63.7 trillion fell significantly short of this guidance due to a more severe memory market downturn, a delayed recovery in foundry demand, and unfavorable foreign exchange rate impacts.

Now to Michael, who will cover operational and product updates.

Michael Rodriguez, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, David.

Let’s revisit the capital expenditure investments from an innovation standpoint:
We launched our new 1alpha nm DRAM node which contributed to a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion for the DRAM sector, driven by a higher average selling price (ASP) and increased unit shipments.

We’ve made strong headway with our inventory management strategy, and expect meaningful results in the second half of 2024. Our inventory management strategy is entering a critical phase of optimization, and we are pleased to report initial progress in line with our previously communicated expectations. As indicated, we anticipate a sequential decline in inventory levels beginning in Q2, a trend we believe will accelerate throughout the remainder of the year. We are employing different strategies based on regional demand and logistical realities. In Europe, where we've experienced slower economic growth, we are actively discounting overstocked items and streamlining our distribution network to reduce carrying costs. Conversely, in the Asia-Pacific region, where demand remains robust, we are focusing on optimizing our inventory mix to ensure we have sufficient stock to meet the continued growth. This includes a targeted marketing campaign to promote high-margin products, effectively reducing the amount of lower-margin products sitting in our inventory.

Let’s move to Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
On wafer ASP, could you expand on the dynamics you're seeing across different DRAM segments?

David Lee:
Absolutely. We believe that while the overall DRAM sector faced ASP declines, the impact varied across segments. Commodity DRAM, specifically DDR4, experienced the most significant ASP erosion, falling by approximately 16%, primarily due to inventory correction and weaker demand in the PC market. High-Performance DRAM, or DDR5, also saw ASPs decline, albeit at a slower pace of around 12%. However, the decline was partly offset by a growing proportion of DDR5 wafers being allocated to server and high-performance computing (HPC) applications, which command premium pricing. Notably, wafer ASP for DDR5 allocated to the server segment remained relatively stable, declining by only 5% due to strong demand for our enterprise solutions. LPDRAM wafer ASPs were relatively more resilient, declining by approximately 10%, with stronger demand for LPDDR5X in high-end smartphones partially offsetting the overall ASP decline.

Analyst 2:
Regarding the inventory reduction strategy, what's the scale and outlook for the second half of the year?

Michael Rodriguez:
We’re seeing momentum with our AI-powered demand forecasting system, especially in North America, which has demonstrably improved forecast accuracy by approximately 12%. We anticipate that the downward trend in inventory levels will accelerate in the second half of the year. We project a further reduction of approximately 8-10% in inventory value by the end of Q3, bringing total inventory to around $1.62 billion. Our target DOI for Q3 is 74 days, with a longer-term goal of reaching 70 days by the end of Q4. This accelerated reduction will be driven by the full implementation of the AI-powered demand forecasting system, the continued expansion of our VMI programs, and the successful execution of our regional optimization strategies. Furthermore, we are implementing a new warehouse management system (WMS) in our key distribution centers during Q3.

Closing

Dr. Anya Sharma:
Thank you all for joining. We’re proud of our progress and excited for what’s ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the call. You may now disconnect.
